title: HADES: Hardware-Assisted Distributed Transactions in the Age of Fast Networks and SmartNICs
problem: Distributed transactional applications suffer from significant software overhead that becomes increasingly apparent as hardware improves with faster networks and powerful NICs. Current software-based transaction systems fail to efficiently leverage modern hardware capabilities.
motivation: Transactional distributed storage applications like key-value stores and databases are widely deployed in cloud systems, making performance improvements directly impactful to cloud infrastructure efficiency.
method: When multiple computers coordinate a transaction (a series of operations that must all succeed or all fail together), most delay comes from software running on CPUs, even though network speeds have improved. HADES offloads transaction coordination to SmartNICs (network interface cards with built-in processors) using Bloom filters (compact data structures that quickly check data membership) to filter transaction requests directly in hardware rather than in software. This hybrid approach accelerates the slowest bottleneck—transaction filtering and coordination—while keeping software handling for flexibility.
key_novelty: HADES embeds Bloom filters in SmartNIC hardware as a core part of the protocol design, enabling transaction validation and coordination to happen at network speeds rather than in software.
contributions: Analysis of software overhead sources in distributed transactional applications
Hardware structures (Bloom filters and SmartNIC support) for efficient transaction support
HADES protocol design leveraging hardware acceleration for low-overhead distributed transactions
Hybrid hardware-software implementation achieving 2.7× throughput improvement over state-of-the-art
